rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up while respecting the program's profile: llubenchmark is a tiny (191 lines, 4 functions) pointer-chasing benchmark whose hot loop is memory-latency-bound, so arithmetic (SUB) and control-flow (BCF, FLA, IBR) transforms add near-noise runtime cost on top of cache-miss-dominated list traversal — hence high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with only moderate RuntimeCost weights. SUB is weighted most aggressively since instruction substitution is essentially free and most reliably breaks pattern-based recovery of the traversal loop. FLA and BCF flatten and pad main's control flow (the 1147-byte hot function) to hide loop structure, with CorrectnessRisk kept low-moderate given round 1's clean result. SPLIT and IGV are raised as cheap size-tolerant diversifiers that fragment basic blocks and obscure global value naming in this minuscule binary where structure is otherwise trivially readable. ICALL is held at moderate weight: with only 4 functions, indirection mostly protects the tiny allocate/_start helpers and adds real call overhead, so it is applied selectively rather than maximally.
